Cartilages and discs: %1$d selectable structures — 23 intervertebral discs, 14 costal structures (ribs 1–7 on each side), 8 laryngeal cartilages, 5 nasal cartilages and the 4 knee menisci. Cartilages and discs retain their skeletal source positions; menisci are aligned to each knee. Costal meshes keep source groupings. Joint-surface cartilage, ear cartilages and the epiglottis are not included. Available ligaments belong to a separate layer. Discs show their outer surface only.
Knee and menisci · OpenStax anatomy textbook
Muscle, muscle part or source group

Muscular layer: %1$d selectable structures, including 52 added head structures. Whole muscles, heads, portions and some groups keep the source nomenclature. This is not a count of individual muscles or a complete muscular system. Eight trunk muscles have been added: paired rectus abdominis, transversus abdominis, quadratus lumborum and pyramidalis. Their registration is approximate, especially at the pelvis and twelfth ribs. Colours are illustrative; tendon fibres and internal tissue are not modelled. Sheets summarize the role of the corresponding muscle family.

Permanent tooth · separate from the bone count

The two-digit label uses FDI notation for permanent teeth. The first digit identifies the quadrant: 1 upper right, 2 upper left, 3 lower left, 4 lower right. The second counts from the midline, from 1 (central incisor) to 8 (wisdom tooth).

The catalogue covers the conventional 206 adult bones. The model represents %1$d of them, plus %2$d additional foot sesamoids (grouped by foot) and %3$d permanent teeth. Teeth are not bones. Individual anatomy and bone counts can vary.

The six middle-ear ossicles and the coccyx have sheets but no separate 3D model here. Wisdom teeth are absent. Cartilages, discs and internal organs have their own layers. Eyes, nervous structures, blood vessels, selected connective tissues and skin have separate layers. The internal microstructure of bones is not represented.

BodyParts3D 4.0 depicts an adult male. These are surface models from the published reduced-polygon dataset: fine details may be simplified. The sternum and hyoid source parts are grouped by bone. This atlas has not undergone independent medical review.

Adaptation: selection of bones, teeth, muscles, cartilages, discs and internal organs, grouping of source parts by anatomical concept, conversion from OBJ to GLB, coordinate conversion, recalculated surface normals and materials. Surface meshes are simplified for mobile rendering, with finer detail retained on small anatomical structures. Organ walls, parenchymal parts and intestinal loops are grouped by organ, excluding overlapping variants and vascular trees. The two identical cricoid source files are deduplicated. Disc FJ3211, labelled generically in the source, is identified spatially at T12–L1 without assigning it a specific FMA identifier. No missing anatomical shape was generated.

The short bilingual sheets are original educational summaries. References include OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology: joints, muscles, endocrine glands, heart, immunity, respiration, digestion, urinary and reproductive organs. Wikipedia links provide further reading; no articles or images are bundled. Source and licence details remain available offline.

Source association corrections: the left/right models of flexor pollicis brevis and middle pharyngeal constrictor are reassigned according to their actual side in the geometry. Their shapes and anatomical identifiers are preserved.

Head and trunk muscles, menisci, lung lobes, thyroid, nerves and lymphoid structures: Z-Anatomy — The libre 3D atlas of anatomy, CC BY-SA 4.0. Gauthier Kervyn (3D and anatomy); Lluís Vinent (FBX distribution). Original model: BodyParts3D — The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan, Kousaku Okubo. Cranial nerves reference: University of Dundee, CAHID, CC BY 4.0.

Adaptation: selection of 52 named head muscle meshes and 4 knee menisci, application of mirrored instances and FBX transformations, conversion to GLB, uniform scale and rigid alignment to the skull or tibial plateaus, recalculated normals and separate materials. Menisci retain their overall source shape, with surfaces simplified for mobile display. The two sources differ in joint pose; small placement discrepancies remain. The combined atlas and adapted Z-Anatomy meshes are distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0; the BodyParts3D 4.0 subset retains its CC BY 4.0 attribution.

The added head muscles are aligned to the skull using a shared scale, rotation and translation. The two source models differ, especially at the mandible; small discrepancies of a few millimetres remain. This alignment has not been clinically validated.
3D rendering: Filament · Google / Android Open Source Project · Apache 2.0.
